call_points.text: H2 guided better than H1, with a return to growth by Q4FY27; Q2 revenue seen flattish.
USD 257 million of wins in Q1FY27, led by connected cars, after-sales transformation and autonomous.
Commercial vehicle revenue to grow next quarter; Q1 dip partly a one-time large license deal in the prior quarter.
Two SDV programs ending: one European program at start of production as planned, one Japanese program cancelled at the last minute.
Other expenses rose on forex, acquisition-related provisions and European subcontracting; CFO called them operational.
Qorix share of loss expected to continue for at least the next quarter or two.
Wage hikes delayed for the first time, to be given in stages starting with younger grades.
Seven off-highway OEMs opened and four truck and bus OEMs engaged to broaden revenue beyond passenger cars.
Tata Motors deal is the N-Dream in-vehicle gaming platform, charged per vehicle under a license model.
Management expects FY27 EBITDA margin between 20.5% to 21.2% after increased investments in AI solutions.
Closed $349 million worth of deal increments during Q4 FY26.
Solution and products revenue growth is targeted at 30% year-on-year.

corporate_actions.subject: Annual General Meeting/Dividend - Rs 1.50 Per Share

guidance.statement: We expect 30% year-on-year revenue growth in solution and products
EBITDA 20.5 to 21.2 post increasing investment in AI solutions
H2 will be better than H1 and the company will return to meaningful growth by Q4FY27
Margins will improve incrementally, not significantly, until revenue returns to growth; 20%+ EBITDA expected by Q4 if growth returns
Commercial vehicle segment to return to growth next quarter

operating_notes.text: Cymotive is an automotive cybersecurity specialist headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, with reported turnover of USD 42.4M in CY2023, USD 32.7M in CY2024, and USD 19.2M in CY2025.
Recommended final dividend of ₹5.25 per equity share (52.5%) for FY26.
KPIT won USD 257 million of deals in Q1FY27, mainly in connected cars, after-sales transformation and autonomous.
Europe is more than 50% of KPIT's revenue, and European OEMs are discussing 30-40% product and production cost reduction with KPIT.
Seven off-highway OEMs and four truck and bus OEMs have been opened as new client engagements to broaden revenue.

timeline.summary: Shrikrishna Patwardhan, promoter, declared no new encumbrances on KPIT Technologies Limited shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) as of April 11, 2026.
On April 29, 2026, KPIT Technologies received approval from NSE and BSE to reclassify two promoters holding 0.82% stake to the public category.
KPIT Technologies approved the acquisition of a strategic stake in Israeli automotive cybersecurity specialist Cymotive Technologies for an initial USD 10 million.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,711 Cr (+12.0% YoY), net profit ₹162.97 Cr.
KPIT Technologies Limited shared the post-earnings investor meet recording link on its website on May 8, 2026, signed by Ashish Malhotra, General Counsel & Company Secretary.
KPIT Technologies reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,711 Cr and outlined its growth strategy in its post-earnings analyst meet transcript.
On 29 July 2026 KPIT's Q1FY27 call reported constant-currency revenue growth of 0.1% YoY, EBITDA margin of 17.2% and PAT of ₹1.17 billion, with management guiding a return to growth only by Q4FY27.
KPIT Technologies scheduled Post Earnings Conference Call on October 28, 2026, at 17:30 IST with Kishor Patil, Sachin Tikekar, Anup Sable, Chinmay Pandit, Priyamvada Hardikar, and Sunil Phansalkar.

watchlist.response: Kishor Patil said the degrowth was because of the top two clients, which are strategic, and one client's decline is not fully reflected yet; CFO said the 87% and 84% figures are percentages of different quarters and should not be compared.
watchlist.text: Strategic clients at 87% of revenue fell only 1.3% QoQ while total USD revenue fell about 4.5%, implying the decline came from non-strategic clients

watchlist.response: Kishor Patil said the impact will come in the next quarter at a regional level, about 4% for the quarter, offset at company level by U.S. and SIMA growth.
watchlist.text: When European OEM revenue decline would show up, since Q1 Europe revenue did not fall as expected

watchlist.response: Kishor Patil said the medium-term outlook remains good, driven by products and solutions and outcome-based models, without giving a revised number.
